newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian oil chief says size of new find unknown.
newsitem.headline: Colombian oil chief says size of new find unknown.

text.p: Colombia's oil chief said on Wednesday he had no idea how much crude oil might be lying in a new field heralded earlier in the day by President Ernesto Samper as an apparent major find.
"There's oil there and of a very good quality," Luis Bernardo Florez, president of the state oil company Ecopetrol, told reporters of the Coporo field, 55 miles (90 km) east of the capital Bogota.

He added, however, that authorities "don't have the slightest idea" how much oil is actually contained in the field since three geological formations still have to be perforated before its potential could be confirmed.

A test well at the site has reached a depth of 17,000 feet (5,100 metres), but the field's potential won't be known until late next month when the well reaches 18,000 feet (5,400 metres), Florez said.
The actual size of the field will be known in about two years time when Ecopetrol finishes drilling two other test wells in the area, Florez said.
Samper told a news briefing on Wednesday in New York, where he was wrapping up a four-day visit to the United Nations, that Coporo could hold up to 700 million barrels in reserves.
But Florez stressed that Samper was only talking about what "geological experts would presume to be the possible existence of 700 million barrels."
He added that Ecopetrol had invested up to $48 million in the Coporo site so far, which is located near the oil-rich Cusiana and Piedemonte fields in Colombia's eastern plains.
